jobs.description:
Firm Overview:
Cambridge Associates (“CA”) is a leading global investment firm. CA’s goal is to help endowments & foundations, pension plans, and ultra-high net worth private clients implement and manage custom investment portfolios that generate outperformance so that they can maximize their impact on the world. Cambridge Associates delivers a range of services, including outsourced CIO, non-discretionary portfolio management, and investment consulting.

Headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts, CA has offices in key markets in North America, the United Kingdom, Europe, Asia, and Oceania.  Our worldwide teams ensure our clients benefit from decades of global presence, local expertise, and relationships with the top global investment managers across the world.  For more information, please visit www.cambridgeassociates.com.

Job Description Summary:
We are hiring an Investment Analyst to join our Investment Strategy Research team in our Singapore office.

Job Description:
Position Overview:
Cambridge Associates’ Investment Strategy Office brings together investment professionals dedicated to market analysis, asset allocation guidance, risk management, and investment science. The Investment Analyst is part of the Investment Strategy Research team, supporting the firm’s research and market analysis work. Working closely with senior colleagues, Analysts gather and assess financial-market data, prepare charts and research materials, and respond to requests from investment teams.

This role offers exposure to a wide variety of asset classes and investment strategies, along with opportunities to develop research and analysis skills. Excellent reading comprehension and written communication skills are required, in addition to quantitative aptitude. Analysts are expected to participate in internal discussions as part of a global team, which may require conference calls outside of normal office hours.

Primary Responsibilities:
- Update and create analysis for use by other departments, ensuring accuracy of data, methodology, and presentation
- Utilize internal AI tools and other internal databases to create and maintain analysis, presentations, and models for internal teams and clients
- Respond to ad hoc requests, upholding our high standards for customer service
- Research new sources of data and become familiar with various data publications and vendors to assist the group in continually expanding data coverage
- Regularly evaluate internal processes to correct inefficiencies, ensure accuracy, and improve communication
- Perform additional duties as necessary to support the firm’s research needs.
- Successful individuals in the role have the opportunity to grow their responsibilities to contribute directly to research, including:
- Working on research pieces alongside Investment Directors, sourcing date, preparing chats, conducting data analysis
- Reading and summarizing leading institutional investment research publications
- Assist in the development and testing of R code designed to accomplish specific task.
- Assist with custom projects requiring quantitative research, financial analysis, and thoughtful modeling.

Qualifications:
- BA/BS degree with a record of high academic achievement. Enrollment in the CFA program a plus
- Fresh graduates and individuals with 0-2 years of similar work experience are welcome to apply
- Analytical ability and intellectual curiosity, with a strong interest in investments and macroeconomics
- Organized with high attention to detail, ability to prioritize and work on multiple projects simultaneously, and work independently and as part of a team
- Proficiency in Microsoft Excel required. Familiarity with Bloomberg, Factset and Thomson Reuters Datastream a plus
- Knowledge of statistical packages such as R, Python is a plus

All applications must include a resume and cover letter.

Pay Range Minimum:
66500 Pay Range Maximum:
76500

Job Description Summary:
Cambridge Associates is a privately held independent investment firm with over $650B in AUA
servicing clients worldwide from our 13 global offices. For more than 50 years, Cambridge
Associates has advised foundations, endowments, private clients, pensions, government
agencies, insurance groups, sovereign wealth funds and healthcare institutions on constructing,
managing, and overseeing their investment assets. The firm was founded in 1973 to serve as an
external research arm to educational endowments, and our investment advisory practice grew out
of this solid research foundation. Today the firm delivers a range of services across asset classes,
including investment advising, discretionary portfolio management, research and investment
tools, and performance monitoring. Our investment teams understand how to identify and evaluate
global investment opportunities and recommend investment strategies that recognize specific
operating and governance issues that institutions face.
We select our colleagues with great attention to their potential to become a valuable member of a
collegial, intelligent and hard-working team.

Job Description:
The Opportunity

We seek a talented individual to join our Retirement, Insurance, and Government practice as a
Senior Investment Director. This role will be an important part of a dynamic team dedicated to
helping clients meet or exceed their investment objectives through thoughtful portfolio
construction, rigorous manager evaluation, and high-quality client service.

Responsibilities

• Construct diversified portfolios with varying investment objectives, policies, and strategic
asset allocation strategies in partnership with senior team members for a sophisticated
client base
• Evaluate investment managers across a broad range of asset classes, including public
equity, fixed income, private investments, and alternative strategies
• Communicate directly with client in-house investment staff, investment committees, and
boards to develop and present investment recommendations and decisions through clear,
high-quality materials
• Prepare analysis, lead and review the preparation of materials for internal discussions and
external client meetings
• Contribute to team efforts across investment strategy, portfolio management, manager
research, marketing, team strategy and business development
• Mentor and oversee junior colleagues in their career development
Qualifications
• BA/BS required; MBA or CFA strongly preferred
• At least 10 years of relevant experience in related role or broader industry
• Intellectually curious, self-motivated, and eager to build experience across investments
and commercial activities
• Experience presenting complex topics to clients with varying levels of sophistication across
both traditional and alternative asset classes
• Familiarly with liability-aware investing is preferred, but not required
• Demonstrated ability to work effectively in a team environment, including experience
mentoring junior colleagues
• Ability to manage competing priorities and adapt effectively as needs evolve
• Strong analytical, technical (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, proprietary systems exposure),
project management, and communication skills
• Comfortable working both independently and as part of a team
• Successfully obtain FINRA Series 3 license within 90 days of employment as  condition of continued employment

jobs.description:

CA’s goal is to help endowments & foundations, pension plans, and ultra-high net worth private clients implement and manage custom investment portfolios that generate outperformance so that they can maximize their impact on the world. Job Description Summary:
Sr. Investment Directors (SDs) on the Venture Capital team spend the majority of their time sourcing, evaluating, and underwriting venture capital investment managers. This includes meeting with managers, attending annual meetings, networking with industry participants to gather market intelligence, and identifying promising new managers. These efforts culminate in conducting due diligence on high-conviction managers for investment by the firm and its clients. The role serves as a primary point of contact for venture capital managers, coordinating and attending meetings, producing written assessments, and facilitating the flow of manager information internally.

In addition, the Sr. Investment Director is responsible for actively monitoring and evaluating managers on an ongoing basis and producing written evaluations for firm and client use. The Sr. Investment Director is also expected to work closely with, and support the development of, Investment Analysts and Associates.

Finally, the Sr. Investment Director will work collaboratively across the broader Cambridge Associates private investments team to track and analyze industry trends, contribute to research and thought leadership, and serve as a resource for client-facing colleagues constructing high-quality private investment portfolios for clients.

Job Description:
Job Responsibilities
·         Lead the investment assessments of venture capital managers and markets through ongoing qualitative and quantitative research and analysis.
·         Utilize common analytical frameworks and develop analyses to assess venture funds in terms of organization, investment strategy, performance, fund terms, portfolio construction, underlying portfolio companies, and other key attributes.
·         Lead meetings with general partners, management teams, founders, and other relevant professionals to assess and evaluate investment managers and their funds.
·         Lead reference calls regarding investment opportunities and market views with industry participants, including founders, portfolio company executives, co-investors, and other market participants.
·         Produce written assessments and recommendations used by clients and colleagues to support investment decisions. For funds, this includes detailed diligence reports backed by meetings, factual analyses, and references; for the market, this includes periodic research reports on current topics of interest.
·         Monitor market trends, fundraising activity, and investment activity, and contribute to the firm’s thought leadership in venture capital.
·         Serve as a resource to colleagues and clients seeking current information on venture capital opportunities and markets, including data and analysis, comparisons across fund managers, and the investment views of the Private Investments team.
·         Prepare materials for and participate in firm-wide meetings in which the private investments team discusses recent manager meetings and current investment opportunities of interest with client-facing colleagues.
·         Represent the firm at annual manager meetings, industry events, and certain meetings with clients and prospects.
·         Contribute to secondaries and co-investment evaluations, when appropriate.
·         Support the development of junior team members through training, collaboration, and apprenticeship.

Qualifications
·         10-12 years of relevant investment experience, with familiarity with venture capital, growth equity, and broader private investments, preferably gained through work at a large institutional investor, venture capital or growth equity firm, or investment advisory firm
·         MBA, CFA, or other relevant professional qualifications strongly preferred
·         Demonstrated understanding of venture capital and its role in a diversified institutional portfolio
·         Demonstrated qualitative and quantitative analytical skills
·         Excellent oral and written communication skills
·         Experience performing relevant financial analysis for private investments and ideally some experience with limited partnership agreements and fund legal terms
·         Ability and willingness to engage directly with managers, founders, executives, and references
·         Ability to prioritize multiple requests for information while ensuring integrity, accuracy, completeness, and timeliness of work
·         Ability to work independently and under time constraints
·         Demonstrated relationship-building skills
·         Strong project management skills
·         Willingness to travel

jobs.description:

Job Description Summary:
The Finance Manager for Technology reports to the Managing Director, Financial Planning & Analysis and serves as the dedicated finance partner to the Technology organization. This is a people-leadership role for an experienced, technically strong finance manager ready to own a function end to end: budgeting, forecasting, cost management, and financial reporting for technology spend. The role shapes the standards for technology financial planning, drives transparency into spend, and supports strategic investment decisions across the IT portfolio.

An important element of this role is building out financial dashboards. The Financial Manager will design and maintain the reporting and visualization tools that turns financial data into self-service insight for business leaders, establishing the key financial indicators, refresh discipline, and data integrity behind them. While the initial focus is technology spend and ROI, this dashboard and reporting work is expected to extend beyond IT to other business areas and firmwide financial reporting over time.

This is a highly visible role that requires a strong blend of financial acumen and technology business knowledge, with regular exposure to IT leadership, Finance, and Executive Management. The ideal candidate works with minimal oversight in a fast-paced, collaborative environment and communicates complex financial information clearly to both finance and non-finance audiences.

Job Description:
Primary Duties
Financial Planning and Budgeting
- Partner with IT leadership to develop and manage the annual technology budget, including capital and operating expenditures across all technology domains.
- Own the monthly and quarterly forecasting processes, identifying variances and separating timing from structural drivers.
- Build and maintain driver-based financial models supporting scenario planning, investment prioritization, and cost optimization.
- Track project financials, including actuals versus budget, capitalization rates, and return on investment, and apply firm-wide budget governance standards.

Dashboards, Reporting and Analysis
- Build and maintain dashboards and recurring reporting for IT leadership, Finance, and senior stakeholders, including materials that feed CFO and Executive Management reviews.
- Analyze spend trends, vendor costs, and headcount-related expenses to identify savings opportunities and efficiency gains.
- Support month-end and year-end close with the Accounting team, and maintain records of IT assets, software licenses, and contracts for reporting and audit requirements.
- Provide ad hoc financial analysis and decision support for strategic initiatives and business cases.

Business Partnership and Process Improvement
- Serve as the primary Finance liaison to IT leadership, translating financial data into clear, actionable insights for non-finance audiences.
- Operate as an embedded participant in technology planning and prioritization forums, business reviews, and initiative governance.
- Collaborate with Procurement and Vendor Management on contract renewals and cost opportunities.
- Lead process improvement and automation of reporting and forecasting workflows, including the practical application of artificial intelligence, and serve as a subject matter expert on IT financial management best practices.
- Support cross-functional initiatives related to technology investment planning, chargeback models, and cost allocation frameworks.

Qualifications and Skills
- BA/BS in Finance, Accounting, or a related field required; MBA preferred.
- 8-12 years of progressive finance experience, including at least 4 years supporting a technology or IT function; asset or wealth management industry background preferred.
- Strong understanding of IT financial management concepts, including capital versus operating expense treatment, software capitalization (ASC 350-40), cost allocation, and technology cost structures such as cloud consumption, software licensing, capitalized development, and contractor versus employee economics.
- Demonstrated experience with budgeting, forecasting, and financial reporting in a complex, matrixed organization.
- Advanced working knowledge of MS Excel is essential (including a full understanding of pivot tables and reference logic) and a basic understanding of MS Access and query logic.
- Hands-on experience building dashboards and reports in business intelligence tools (e.g., Power BI, Tableau) and AI platforms.
- Proficiency with financial planning tools and ERP systems (e.g., Oracle EPM, Hyperion, Anaplan, Workday, SAP); experience with IT financial management platforms a plus.
- Proven ability to lead projects and processes independently and influence decisions across functions without formal authority.
- Strong oral, written, and presentation skills; able to produce executive-ready materials that lead with insight, paired with a definitive emphasis on quality control: numbers tie, formats are clean, and nothing goes unchecked.
- Highly organized, adaptable, and self-motivated; works well with new or ambiguous information, competing priorities, and visible senior exposure while maintaining accuracy.
- Strong team orientation, enjoys rolling up sleeves to resolve complex undertakings, and holds the highest standards of honesty, integrity, and confidentiality.

Job Description Summary:
The Opportunity
The Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A) Financial Analyst – Shared Services is responsible for monthly and quarterly financial reporting, forecast, annual budget and ad hoc analysis for business partners across the firm. This is a hands-on role with an emphasis on performing financial analysis that provides senior management with insights needed to make strategic decisions around expenses. A strong communicator and team player, this role will work closely with peers in Finance & Accounting and across the business to build strong and collaborative partnerships across Accounting & Finance, Legal, Human Capital and other corporate functions.

Job Description:
Responsibilities
Financial Planning & Analysis
- Partner with Accounting & Finance, Legal, Human Capital and other corporate function leaders to build the annual budget and complete monthly forecasts
- Maintain and enhance financial models within the enterprise planning tool, ensuring data integrity across cost centers
- Analyze headcount, vendor spend, and departmental cost trends and deliver monthly variance analysis (actuals vs. budget/forecast) with clear, actionable commentary

Business Partnering
- Prepare monthly/quarterly P&L reviews, dashboards, and executive-ready summaries for Shared Services leadership
- Serve as the primary financial point of contact for assigned corporate functions, translating financial data into operational insight
- Support ad hoc analyses for leadership, including cost-benefit analysis, scenario planning, and resource allocation decisions

Continuous Improvement & Technology Adoption
- Proactively identify opportunities to streamline reporting and forecasting processes — reducing manual effort and cycle time
- Champion the adoption of AI-powered tools (e.g., AI for enhanced reporting, automation for data reconciliation, anomaly detection in spend data) within the FP&A function
- Partner with Financial Systems teams to optimize configuration and functionality of the enterprise planning/forecasting tool

Qualifications
- 5+ years of FP&A / budgeting / forecasting experience preferred
- Advanced proficiency in MS Excel (e.g. INDEX MATCH; complex SUMIF, Pivot Tables, V/H Lookups)
- Experience with Enterprise Planning tools (e.g., Oracle EPM)
- Able to manage complex financial data
- Strong and well-rounded project management experience, time management skills, attention to detail and ability to multi-task with often competing priorities
- Excellent communication skills; able to express complex thoughts clearly and convincingly in writing, in-person, and in group settings
- Self-starter constantly seeking and identifying process improvements and efficiencies
- Proven expertise in financial modeling and data analytics
- Service orientated with motivation to serve and support stakeholders
- Familiarity with Accounting principles

Job Description Summary:
This is a senior commercial leadership role focused on business development, high-quality pipeline generation, and market expansion. The Managing Director will originate, qualify, cultivate, and support conversion of new business opportunities across family offices, private clients, foundations, pensions, and other institutional investors.
This individual will engage directly with senior decision makers, centers of influence, and strategic referral sources, helping shape regional business development strategy and translating market intelligence into actionable growth plans. The role requires strong commercial acumen, relationship building skills, credibility with sophisticated investors, and the ability to communicate complex investment concepts clearly and effectively to a range of audiences.

Job Description:
Key Responsibilities
- Lead the business development strategy for Geneva and French speaking Switzerland, with scope to support broader Swiss and selected EMEA growth initiatives.
- Represent Cambridge Associates as a senior market facing leader across the region through direct outreach, meetings, conferences, and targeted relationship building activity such as local events.
- Proactively identify and pursue new opportunities across family offices, private clients, pensions, foundations, endowments, and other institutional segments.
- Develop a targeted relationship development plan for key prospect segments and referral channels.
- Establish and deepen relationships with key centers of influence, including consultants, private banks, lawyers, fiduciaries, trustees, and other market participants.
- Build and manage a high quality pipeline of prospects, with disciplined tracking of opportunity stage, activity, timing, and revenue potential.
- Engage directly with prospects to understand their objectives, governance structures, and investment needs, and position Cambridge Associates’ solutions effectively.
- Collaborate with practice wide business development programs to leverage firm wide networks, including existing clients, investment managers, and strategic partners.
- Partner with investment, client solutions, and marketing teams to shape messaging, investment strategy development specific to regional needs.
- Use investment and portfolio knowledge to engage credibly with sophisticated prospects and stakeholders on complex topics.
- Maintain strong CRM discipline and provide regular commercial updates and market insight to senior leadership.
- Help strengthen Cambridge Associates’ long term business development capabilities and market presence in Switzerland.

Candidate Profile
- Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree or professional qualification such as an MBA, CFA, or equivalent preferred.
- Minimum 15 years of experience in business development, investment consulting, wealth management, investment management, or a related field.
- Proven track record of originating and converting new business opportunities and building a measurable sales pipeline.
- Strong knowledge of the Swiss market, especially Geneva and French speaking Switzerland, with established relationships across relevant client and referral networks.
- Experience working with family offices, private clients, foundations, pensions, and institutional investors is highly desirable.
- Excellent communication, presentation, and interpersonal skills, with strong commercial judgment and the ability to operate effectively in a matrixed organization.
- Fluency in English and French is required; additional regional language capabilities are a plus.

Location and Travel
This role is based in Geneva. Willingness to travel within the region and more broadly as needed is required.
Potential for Broader Swiss Leadership
Over time, the successful candidate may have the opportunity to contribute to the executive committee and or management board of Cambridge Associates’ Swiss firm.
